text:
**Bottom line:** Sit-stand desks did not measurably improve afternoon work output in this 12-week study of 214 office workers. Typing and proofreading speed and accuracy were no different from those with standard desks.

**Benefits found:** Back discomfort was lower (31% vs 44%), and 78% of the sit-stand group felt more productive.

**Caveats:** Extra standing dropped from 47 minutes a day in week 2 to 19 minutes by week 12, so the novelty appears to fade. The task was short and may not reflect real work, and participants knew which desk they had.
